title: Whipped by his father for playing Alozo's at fifteen
summary: As a boy he played at a house in New Iberia with his cousin and was punished by his father.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I know you weren't playing. Oh, oh, oh. I tell you I got a beating for that. I mean a good win for that. Yes, indeed. I went and played at the place they used to call Alozo's in New Iberia. I was quite a lad. I was only fifteen years old. And when I came here, somebody went there with my cousin, and somebody told my father that I played in Napoleon's place, he said, where at? They said, Alozo's. What was you doing in Alozo? I said, well I didn't know any better, I just went there with my cousin Richard. And everybody said, all right, come on over here. Next time you go to New Iberia, you don't go to those places, you ain't got no business there. And believe me, I was afraid of

those places from that day on. Tell me, did you notice in the people that you associated with sort of an attitude of looking down their nose at you because you were a jazz player, did you meet any of that at all in New Orleans? Well that's good. I'm glad they didn't. I know in North Louisiana, how I was raised in a very strict Protestant atmosphere. All of this was looked upon as being highly sinful and so on, you know.
